text.content:
NORTHBRIDGE TODAY — Staff Magazine

Cutting Packaging Waste at the Distribution Center

Last quarter, Northbridge Logistics launched a pilot program to reduce cardboard waste at its Riverside distribution center. Teams replaced oversized boxes with right-sized packaging and introduced reusable plastic totes for local deliveries.
Early results have been [[151]]. Material costs fell by nearly 12%, and fewer damaged shipments were reported. [[152]], drivers noted that the lighter totes were easier to load.

Managers plan a [[153]] rollout to two additional centers in January. [[154]]

Employees with suggestions may email greenops@northbridge.example.

questions.explanation: Context (cost savings and fewer damaged shipments) shows positive results. "Encouraging" means promising or favorable.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing "discouraging," the opposite sense, or another adjective that does not fit the positive data.

questions.explanation: The drivers' comment adds another positive outcome. "Moreover" is the additive discourse marker.
questions.commonMistake: Using "In contrast" when the sentence continues the good-news pattern rather than opposing it.

questions.explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun "rollout." "Gradual" correctly modifies "rollout."
questions.commonMistake: Choosing the adverb "gradually" where an adjective slot before a noun is required.

text.content:
Dear Mr. Okonkwo,

Thank you for contacting Apex Home Goods about order #AH-44921. We apologize for the delay in delivering your kitchen appliance set.
Our records show that the package left the warehouse on time. [[155]], a regional carrier backlog held the shipment at a sorting facility for three extra days.
The items are now out for delivery and should arrive by tomorrow evening. As a courtesy, we have applied a 10% [[156]] to your account for use on a future purchase.

Please accept our [[157]] for the inconvenience. [[158]]

Sincerely,
Priya Nair
Customer Care Specialist
Apex Home Goods

questions.explanation: The carrier backlog is bad news after saying the package left on time. "Unfortunately" signals that disappointing turn.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing "Similarly" or "For instance," which do not mark an adverse development.

questions.explanation: In customer service, a store "credit" is money or value applied to an account for a future purchase.
questions.commonMistake: Picking a similar-looking noun (credential / critique) that does not mean account credit.

questions.explanation: After the possessive "our," a noun is required. "Apology" is the noun form in "accept our apology."
questions.commonMistake: Using the verb "apologize" after "our," where a noun is needed.

text.content:
MEMORANDUM

To: All department managers
From: Finance Department
Date: September 8
Subject: Revised policy for travel expense reimbursement

Effective October 1, employees must submit travel expense reports within ten business days of returning from a trip. Reports filed after that window will require director-level [[159]] before payment can be processed.
Itemized receipts remain mandatory for lodging, airfare, and meals above $25. [[160]], mileage claims must use the rate published on the intranet; handwritten estimates will no longer be accepted.

Please share this update with your teams and [[161]] that staff complete the short policy quiz by September 25. [[162]]

Questions may be directed to finance-help@firm.example.
— Controllers Office

questions.explanation: Late reports need director-level "approval" (authorization) before Finance pays them.
questions.commonMistake: Confusing similar nouns (approach / appearance) that do not mean authorization to pay.

questions.explanation: The mileage rule is an additional requirement alongside itemized receipts. "Furthermore" adds that policy point.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing "Conversely," which would introduce an opposite idea rather than another rule.

questions.explanation: Parallel to "share," the base-form verb "ensure" is needed after "Please … and."
questions.commonMistake: Using "ensuring" (gerund/participle) where a parallel imperative verb is required.

passages.title: Voluntary recall of AquaPure pitcher filters

text.content:
NOTICE

Voluntary Product Recall — AquaPure Pitcher Filters (Lot AP-228)

The Quality Assurance team has confirmed a sealing defect in AquaPure pitcher filters from lot AP-228. Units from this lot were shipped to retailers between June 3 and June 20. The affected cartridges may [[163]] to reduce chlorine to the level stated on the label.
Customers who purchased lot AP-228 should discontinue use at once. [[164]], unused cartridges may be returned to any participating store for a full refund or a replacement from a later lot.

Replacement inventory is [[165]] to reach retail shelves by July 8. [[166]]

Questions about store credit or shipping labels may be sent to recall@aquapure.example.
— Product Safety Office

questions.explanation: After the modal "may," the base-form verb is required. "Fail to reduce" is the correct verb phrase.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing the noun "failure" or the participle "failing" after a modal verb.

questions.explanation: The return-and-refund option is the logical result of the defect and the order to stop using the filters. "Therefore" marks that consequence.
questions.commonMistake: Using "In contrast" when the notice is stating a result, not an opposing idea.

questions.explanation: "Are expected to reach" means the replacements are scheduled or anticipated to arrive by July 8.
questions.commonMistake: Selecting a look-alike verb (excepted / extracted / expired) that does not mean "scheduled to arrive."

text.content:
Dear Ms. Okada,

Thank you for meeting with our purchasing team last Thursday to review next year’s supply of recycled copier paper. We were glad to confirm that Linden Paper will remain our primary vendor.

As agreed, Linden will deliver 200 cases to our Riverdale warehouse each month, beginning January 6. Pricing in the attached schedule will remain [[167]] for the full calendar year unless both parties sign a written amendment.
Standard terms require payment within 30 days of invoice. [[168]], accounts that settle within ten days will receive a 1.5% prompt-payment discount.

Please sign and return the enclosed agreement by October 15 so that we can [[169]] the contract before the budget closes. [[170]]

We look forward to another year of reliable service.

Sincerely,
Hector Ruiz
Purchasing Manager
Oak & Pine Furnishings

questions.explanation: Prices that stay in effect for the year "remain valid" unless a written amendment changes them.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing a similar-looking adjective (vacant / vague / vain) that does not mean "still in force."

questions.explanation: The ten-day discount is an exception to the standard 30-day payment rule. "However" signals that contrast.
questions.commonMistake: Using "Similarly" or "For example" when the sentence introduces a special exception, not a parallel or sample case.

questions.explanation: After "we can," a base-form verb is required. "Finalize the contract" means complete it officially.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing the adjective "final" or the adverb "finally" where a verb slot is needed.
